business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Brokerage of Ginned Raw Cotton and Synthetic Yarns

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 1258 of 2008 (SAS); Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF); Law 1121 of 2006; Decree 1068 of 2015; Superintendencia de Sociedades External Circular 100-000005 of 2021 (SAGRILAFT); DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2021 as amended by Resolution 000095 of 2022 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales or RUBF)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and registry extract of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by home jurisdiction; if non-Hague state, Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Good standing certificate of the foreign shareholder (certificado de vigencia)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction corporate registrar or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special power of attorney granted by foreign shareholders to the local incorporator or legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Colombian consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by registration with the Colombian Chamber of Commerce

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports of each foreign shareholder, director and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or consular legalization, with certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of ultimate beneficial owner and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each shareholder or UBO, signed before Colombian notary or home-country notary if abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille for foreign execution; notarization in Colombia for domestic execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and standard KYC/AML compliance attestation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with certified Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives and UBOs against OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated sanctions, and Colombian UIAF national risk indicators. PEPs are flagged and subjected to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval. The SAGRILAFT manual must incorporate a risk-based CDD policy, ongoing transaction monitoring, and mandatory reporting of unusual operations to UIAF under Law 526 of 1999.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) – www.rues.org.co, operated jointly with local Cámaras de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be drafted in Spanish and in Latin script. Names derived from foreign languages must be transliterated phonetically into Spanish and explained in the articles of incorporation. The name must end with the suffix 'S.A.S.' and may not suggest a different corporate form or instrumentality of the state.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 30 business days and may be extended once for an additional 30 business days if application is made before expiry. If the chosen name is rejected, the incorporator may file the administrative remedies of recurso de reposición before the same Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days, followed by recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio. Alternatively, the incorporator may resubmit a new homonymy search with a modified proposed name without prejudice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for SAS registration, including low-risk international brokerage activities. A virtual office contract or sublease authorization must be filed with the Chamber of Commerce, and the address must be physically located within the jurisdiction. The company must be able to receive judicial notices, tax correspondence, and service of process. A P.O. box alone is not sufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for this export brokerage activity: approximately 5% annual baseline. The likelihood increases to approximately 15% if a virtual office is used instead of a dedicated physical office, because the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN may perform spot checks to verify the existence and operational substance of the registered office.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and homonymy search before the Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory chamber tariff for name certification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the private incorporation document and certified signatures of incorporators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Colombian notarial tariff for private document legalization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Merchant registration of the S.A.S. and filing of the incorporation document with the Chamber of Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chamber registration fee, excluding registration tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration tax on registered capital (impuesto de registro)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Departamental treasury of the registered office jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Approximately 0.7% of registered initial capital, applied to de minimis startup capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign apostilled corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per certified translation unit

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of foreign corporate documents and powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille authority in country of origin / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee; excludes courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular or notarial execution of the general and special power of attorney
Initial RUBF beneficial owner registration filing with DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Electronic filing has no statutory fee; compliance agent fee for preparation and submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAGRILAFT AML/CFT risk manual and compliance procedures
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee for a low-risk international brokerage company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered virtual office annual fee including mail handling and service-of-process acceptance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-46; Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio) Article 110 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del lugar del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce of the municipality of registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued upon registration of the private incorporation document (Documento Privado de Constitución) in the Mercantile Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capitalization; Law 1258 permits S.A.S. formation without minimum capital, but at least one share must be subscribed and fully paid for each class of shares issued; capital may be expressed and paid in foreign currency at authorized exchange rates. Escrow rules do not apply unless cash contributions are deferred; unpaid subscriptions must be recorded and settled within 3 years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution of Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada: The sole founding shareholder resolves to approve the initial share subscription of the subscribed capital of the company, accepting all issued shares. The registered office is adopted at the domicile address stated in the bylaws. The following officers are appointed for the first statutory term: one legal representative, one substitute legal representative, and one accountant. The appointed legal representative is expressly authorized to execute all filings before the Chamber of Commerce, the tax authority (DIAN), and any public registry, and to complete all formalities required for the company to commence its commercial operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Name Availability and Obtain Homonymy Certificate (Certificado de Homonimia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application through the online virtual office (RUES) or at the Chamber's customer service window with the preferred corporate name. The Chamber verifies that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and issues a negative homonymy certificate valid for 30 days. The certificate must be referenced in the incorporation document.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the shareholder (if natural person)
Tax identification number (NIT/RUT) if previously assigned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a reconsideration petition with the Chamber or select an alternative name and re-request the certificate without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Private Incorporation Document (Acta de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional; not mandatory unless asset transfers) and the founding shareholder(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company bylaws in Spanish, including corporate name, domicile, share classes and rights, subscribed and paid capital, duration, internal governance rules, audit requirements, dissolution causes, and appointment of officers. The document may be executed as a private deed. If the S.A.S. is formed by sole shareholder, sign a unilateral unilateral declaration of incorporation. Notarization is required only when contributions of real estate or in-kind assets exceeding a statutory threshold are made; for brokerage-only operations private execution suffices.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney (if acting through agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber identifies errors in the bylaws, correct the document and resubmit; no formal rectification procedure is required prior to registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the S.A.S. in the Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil de la Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document together with the homonymy certificate, the RUT of the company (if pre-assigned) or initial tax identification form, and the completed registration form (Formulario de Registro). Pay statutory registration fees and the commercial registry tax. The Chamber registers the company and issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which is the official proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Incorporation document (private deed or public deed if notarized)
Proof of payment of registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried due to missing annexures, file supplementary documents within 5 business days; the Chamber will re-assess and may issue the certificate within 2 days after cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the DIAN online portal to complete the pre-registration form before the Chamber registration in order to obtain a provisional NIT. After the Chamber issues the certificate, finalize the RUT registration by informing the principal economic activity (ISIC 4620), tax classification (Responsable de IVA, if applicable), and export status. Submit the certificate of existence and representation, the legal representative's identification, and proof of registry fees.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
RUT pre-registration form printed from DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DIAN rejects the RUT application due to mismatched information, correct the data and re-submit electronically; a new application may be required if the NIT is blocked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register Foreign Investment and Shareholders (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank) / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If any equity contribution is made by a non-resident in foreign currency or through a capital movement, file the declaration of foreign investment with the Central Bank within the first 30 days after incorporation using the electronic foreign exchange system. Submit the certification of the legal representative, the shareholders' foreign investment identity documents, and the banking proof of the capital remittance received through a Colombian commercial bank.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Power of attorney of foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is objected, submit the corrected form with supporting bank records; the Central Bank will confirm the registration and issue the foreign investment certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Social Security and Parafiscal System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) and Administradoras de Fondos de Pensiones & EPS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the company has employees or once the legal representative is registered as a contributing spouse/administrator, the company must register as an employer with the integrated contribution settlement operator and register workers with the relevant EPS (health), ARL (workplace risk), and pension fund. This step is mandatory to obtain the occupational health and safety clearance certificate required for operation.
required_dossiers: Worker registration list and labor contract drafts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is rejected, contact the social security operator to reconcile worker identification data and re-submit the contribution form.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades (for commercial oversight) and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT) – no industrial manufacturing permit required for brokerage-only operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license or manufacturing permit is statutorily required for the international brokerage of raw cotton bales (ISIC 4620); export of raw cotton bales does not require a specific industrial license, but the company must obtain an RUT and, if carrying out warehouse storage, a municipal commercial operating permit (Matrícula Mercantil activity registration) is sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) acting under the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category III (no comprehensive environmental license required for commercial brokerage and warehouse activities without transformation; no EIA report needed).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If warehouses are used, compliance with Resolution 909 of 2008 (stationary source emissions), Resolution 0631 of 2015 (discharge limits to surface waters), and Law 1259 of 2008 (plastic straw waste policy) for solid waste handling; cotton bales must be stored on clean pallets, avoid thermoplastic contamination, and waste fibers must be disposed of under municipal waste management rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) for any rented storage area; structural load inspection of the administrative office floor versus seismic resistant building code (NSR-10); occupational health and workplace risk clearance from the ARL and EPS forms confirming compliance with Decree 1072 of 2015 (Chapter 6, Occupational Health and Safety Management System).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — National Tax and Customs Directorate; primary e-services portal: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) at https://www.muisca.dian.gov.co; institutional portal: https://www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A locally incorporated S.A.S. obtains its NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) automatically upon registration with the Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio), followed by mandatory inscription in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) through MUISCA using the DIAN's virtual office; the S.A.S. must complete the RUT form with ISIC 4620 activity, obtain an electronic signature (firma electrónica) and password, and update the RUT within ten (10) business days of any relevant change. A non-resident foreign entity without a Colombian establishment that has any local tax obligation (e.g., obtaining refundable VAT credits) must also obtain an NIT under DIAN Resolution No. 000007 of 2021 by submitting apostilled/legalized incorporation documents, appointing an attorney-in-fact domiciled in Colombia, and completing the electronic RUT pre-registration in MUISCA; the DIAN issues the NIT after validating beneficial ownership, representative authority, and the economic activity code.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (S.A.S.) is a capital company with separate legal personality subject to corporate income tax (CIT) at the entity level; it is not fiscally transparent and does not permit pass-through of income to shareholders. A Colombian-resident S.A.S. is taxed on worldwide income, while non-resident sellers deriving Colombian-source income are taxed on a territorial basis. Exports of goods are outside the preferential Tax-Exempt Zone (Zona Franca) regime unless an explicit DIAN authorization is obtained; the standard S.A.S. with ISIC 4620 export trading activities is therefore taxable as a general-regime resident company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not implement the U.S. check-the-box regime or any elective pass-through treatment for S.A.S. entities; hybrid mismatch and CFC rules under Law 2277 of 2022 apply mandatorily with no opt-out elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) classification as a common-regime or simplified-regime VAT responsible party where statutory thresholds are met and the taxpayer is not an exporter; (ii) election to be taxed under the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE/SIMPLESR) for eligible small entities whose revenue is below the UVT ceilings and that do not engage in export operations; (iii) election to request DIAN's discretionary 'Gran Contribuyente' authorization; and (iv) election to claim excess VAT credits through refund (devolución) versus set-off (compensación) under Articles 815 and 850 of the Colombian Tax Statute (Estatuto Tributario).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Impuesto sobre las Ventas (IVA); general indirect tax regime codified in Articles 420–481 of the Estatuto Tributario, as amended by Law 2010 of 2019 and Law 2277 of 2022.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for exporters: any person carrying out taxable transactions or export operations must register in the RUT and obtain responsible-party status in the VAT common regime from the first transaction. The simplified-regime ceiling of 3,500 UVT (approximately COP 174,296,500 for tax year 2025, with UVT at COP 49,799) is not available to exporters, who are statutorily excluded from the simplified regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing: all sales, including exports, must be documented using the electronic sales invoice (factura electrónica de venta – FE) and transmitted to DIAN for pre-validation before the invoice is legally issued; the invoice must carry the CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) and an XML schema validated through a DIAN-authorized technology provider (proveedor tecnológico) or directly via MUISCA APIs. Export operations additionally require electronic transmission of the export declaration (DEX e-export), use of the applicable document-support mechanism (documento soporte) for acquisitions from non-invoicing suppliers, and compliance with the DIAN's 2024–2025 invoice validation resolution requiring acceptance or rejection responses within the regulated period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including ginned raw cotton bales) are statutorily excluded (excluidas) from VAT under Article 424 ET and effectively benefit from a 0% VAT liability, provided: (a) the goods physically leave the Colombian customs territory and the national export declaration (DEX) has obtained 'levante' (release) in the customs system; (b) the purchaser is a foreign user located abroad and the goods are not reintroduced into Colombia; (c) the sale is duly invoiced with the electronic export invoice; and (d) the exporter maintains contemporaneous evidence of transport (bill of lading/air waybill), payment terms, and FX repatriation. Zero-rating of services requires the additional export-service conditions of Article 481 ET and Article 22 of Decree 1625 of 2016, including the benefit-obtained-abroad test and the full-use-abroad requirement; these rules do not apply to the present goods-export scope.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Declaración de Exportación (DEX) transmitted electronically (e-export) with DIAN 'levante' release authorization
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing physical shipment and destination
Inward Remittance Certificate — Declaración de Cambio por Exportaciones (Form No. 3) evidencing FX repatriation and settlement through an authorized foreign-exchange intermediary
Commercial Invoice (factura comercial) / electronic export invoice containing the CUFE code
Packing List (lista de empaque) matching marks, weights, and bale count
Certificate of Origin (documento de origen) where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
Pre-shipment inspection certificate when required by the letter of credit, contract, or ISIC 4620 trade practice
Transit and final-destination documentation where the goods pass through third-country ports or free zones
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits export VAT exclusions at the customs-vs-fiscal level, cross-matching the DEX declarations, electronic export invoices, and the FX 'reintegro' (repatriation) records filed with the authorized intermediaries. If the exclusion is overturned or the refund application is found improper, the taxpayer must repay the VAT credit claimed plus default interest, with the following penalties: (i) a 100% penalty for tax inaccuracy in amended returns (Art. 647 ET); (ii) a 20% penalty for improper refunds or compensations (Art. 670 ET); (iii) a 200% penalty where deliberate distortion or concealment is established; (iv) criminal liability for export smuggling and fraudulent export declarations under Law 1762 of 2015, with imprisonment penalties of up to eight (8) years, extended for criminal organizations; and (v) administrative closure of customs authorized-economic-operator (OEA) status, suspension of export registration, and disqualification from future VAT refund proceedings in the case of repeated violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia, acting as the central bank and foreign-exchange administrator, together with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (financial conduct supervision) and the Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo for trade-related FX matters. The applicable normative core is Law 9 of 1991 (Estatuto Cambiario) and Banco de la República's external foreign-exchange regulation (Circular Reglamentaria Externa DCIN 83-3, Chapters 7 and 10).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime with unrestricted current-account convertibility for imports, exports, services, and profit remittances. Dividend and branch remittances by a Colombian S.A.S. to non-resident shareholders do not require prior central-bank approval, subject only to: (i) prior registration of the inbound foreign direct investment with Banco de la República via the Declaración de Inversión Internacional (Form 4); (ii) settlement through the Colombian FX market (mercado cambiario) using an authorized intermediary; and (iii) payment of the applicable dividend withholding tax (7.5% statutory rate, reduced where a Colombia tax treaty applies) on the taxable dividend. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections, shareholder loans, and portfolio commitments, are liberalized and do not require administrative pre-authorization, but all dispositions of foreign currency must be routed through authorized commercial banks or financial corporations. Profit remittances exceedable only on the declared, audited, and tax-paid accounting basis.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under DCIN 83-3, for goods exports, including raw cotton bales (ISIC 4620 / NAICS 424590), where the invoice value per export shipment equals or exceeds USD 50,000 or the aggregate of consecutive shipments reaches the same threshold, the full export proceeds must be channeled into the Colombian foreign-exchange market through an authorized intermediary. Statutory term: the proceeds must be received and presented to the intermediary within six (6) months counted from the customs export date (confrontada la salida); extensions to eight (8) months are possible for specific export lists upon Banco de la República approval. Conversion to COP is not mandatory: the exporter may maintain the USD balance in a foreign-currency deposit account (Cuenta de Depósito en Moneda Extranjera) at the same authorized bank. The channeling ratio is 100% of the declared export value; any non-channeled surplus is treated as unlawful FX subject to monetary fines (up to 200% of the non-repatriated amount). The exporter must complete the Informe Cambiario de Presentación de Divisas (bank-declaration form) at the time of the collection and retain supporting proof (bill of lading, commercial invoice, FMM/customs exit manifest, SWIFT MT103 credit advice, and broker commission schedule) for a minimum of five (5) years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational COP current account + USD foreign-currency deposit account (Cuenta de Depósito en Moneda Extranjera), optionally a specialized capital-contribution account for foreign investment escrow
Capital Escrow Account (custodia de aportes de capital) used for the registered foreign investment, plus COP operational account for trade disbursements
Operational checking account in COP with cross-border trade desk; foreign-currency deposit account available for export proceeds
International trade settlement account (USD-denominated) with documentary LC facility, domiciled at the Bogotá corporate banking unit
Corporate operational account (COP) and import/export settlements account (USD) with FX derivative facility
Operational checking account (Cuenta Corriente) in COP; USD account available subject to commodity-trade program approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Colombian fintech payment institutions operate strictly as SEDPES (Sociedades Especializadas en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos) and may transact only in COP, with restricted wallet balances and no FX intermediation. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, Airwallex) are not authorized intermediaries under the Colombian FX regime and cannot lawfully receive or settle the export proceeds of a Colombian S.A.S. without violating the channeling obligation. Their use is limited to ancillary Euro/USD corporate expense cards and third-country procurement disbursements; the statutory clearing and collection of raw cotton export receivables must remain at a Tier-1 authorized bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Colombian S.A.S. with non-resident shareholders or directors, Tier-1 institutions mandate a two-fold onboarding: (i) a remote videoconference KYC interview of the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owners, and (ii) a physical verification of the registered seat and, in practice, a one-time in-person or notarized action in Bogotá or Medellín by the legal representative or a resident attorney-in-fact holding apostilled powers of attorney. Fully remote opening without any local touchpoint is not accepted by the indicated Tier-1 banks; the participation of a Colombian resident compliance contact materially improves approval rates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and opaque UBO chain over the S.A.S. (common red flag for shell-structure screening)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled incorporation deed (documento privado de constitución) and bylaws; Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the Cámara de Comercio (issued within 30 days); RUT (Registro Único Tributario) evidencing 35, 42, and 4620 tax and industry registrations; final-beneficiary declaration filed to the bank under the Colombian LA/FT risk-management framework; audited or reviewed financial statements for the last two (2) years; business plan describing the cotton-brokerage corridor, suppliers, and target buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First-time high-value USD flows inbound/outbound inconsistent with the company's assets and early-stage balance sheet
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed international sale-purchase contracts for raw cotton bales (ISIC 4620), dedicated warehouse receipts and bills of lading, origin and quality certificates from ginning authorities, full invoice-payment corridor (supplier purchase invoice to buyer sales invoice), tax clearance certificate (Paz y Salvo), and the legal representative's wealth and source-of-funds declaration corroborated by bank statements of the related entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or jurisdiction heat-mapping triggered on counterparty banks/ginners in the cotton supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screening justification memo evidencing compliant counterparty due diligence; OECD-grain/cotton-commodity trade-compliance attestations; irrevocable documentary LC or confirmed CAD documentation to anchor the true economic purpose; commitment letter restricting transactions with blocked persons and requiring bank approval for any third-country beneficiary change.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders subscribe and pay capital (capital mínimo is not mandatory, but the subscribed capital declared in the deed must be paid below USD 10,000 without formality; larger injections require formal payment). Each equity wire must be sent via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the S.A.S.'s account at an authorized bank, quoting: (i) beneficiary name exactly matching the RUT; (ii) purpose code 'Formación de Inversión Internacional – Aportes de Capital' (Direct Foreign Investment); and (iii) reference to the shareholder subscription minutes. The receiving bank is obliged to file the declaración cambiaria; the company must register the transaction on Form 4 (Declaración de Inversión Internacional) with Banco de la República within the statutory window (six months from payment, before any dividend remittance or disposal) and obtain the certificate of registration, which also supports future dividend outflows. Wire-funding through unlicensed third-party EMI channels is prohibited; cash deposits and cryptocurrency bridging are not acceptable FX-channel evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the cotton-bale trade: (1) Supplier payments to overseas ginners and freight providers: SWIFT MT103/MT202 through the authorized bank using the applicable import/export purpose code (e.g., 'Importación de mercancías' for the purchase leg, 'Fletes y seguros' for logistics), with the six-month export-proceeds channeling obligation applied to the earned foreign currency; (2) Export receipts from buyers: presented under irrevocable sight/tenor documentary letters of credit governed by UCP 600, or by documentary collection (D/P or D/A) governed by URC 522, with the confirming Colombian bank crediting the USD foreign-currency deposit account and completing the divisa presentment form; (3) For intra-group or recurring corridors, standing netting of payables and receivables in a foreign currency deposit account is permitted but must never extinguish the statutory channeling duty on the collection leg. All outbound drafts, quality certificates, bills of lading, and certificates of origin must be consigned to the negotiating bank to keep the LC clean.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable COP/USD forward contracts (compraventa a término) with authorized intermediaries of Banco de la República, maturing up to 180 days, back-to-back with the underlying cotton export receivable
Non-deliverable forwards (COP NDF) referenced to the TRM (Tasa Representativa del Mercado), permitted for resident exporters as a hedge for uncovered USD receivables
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD) for the conversion of long-term EUR or USD-denominated trade liabilities into COP, executed exclusively with banks authorized by Banco de la República
COP/USD futures listed on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (BVC) for standardized tenors plus OTC options on the TRM used solely for hedging the cotton brokerage margin

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (Commercial Registry Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce at the registered office jurisdiction)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 31 for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of 1–5 times the legal minimum monthly wage (SMMLV) per infraction; continued non-renewal for three consecutive years may trigger administrative strike-off of the commercial registration. Filing after the deadline also exposes the entity to restriction from conducting certain business and financing operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales (Annual UBO Notification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales), filed via Cámara de Comercio or DIAN electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 (aligned with the commercial renewal cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DIAN penalties: fine up to 5% of the taxpayer's equity or 1,000 SMMLV (whichever is less), plus inability to obtain tax clearance and credit certificates. Repeated non-compliance may trigger ineligibility for government procurement and foreign trade benefits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is required if any of the following conditions are met: (i) total assets at prior year-end exceed 5,000 SMMLV; (ii) gross income for the prior fiscal year exceeds 3,000 SMMLV; (iii) the company employs more than 30 workers; or (iv) the entity qualifies as a public-interest entity under Colombian regulations. For 2025, 1 SMMLV = COP 1,423,500. A SAS below these thresholds may still appoint a Revisor Fiscal voluntarily.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs (Group 2) generally applies to small and medium enterprises; full IFRS (Group 1) applies to listed, public-interest, or large entities; simplified local accounting framework (Group 3) applies to micro-enterprises. Financial statements must be prepared and approved jointly by the shareholders' meeting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must submit the annual UBO declaration even if no beneficial ownership changes occurred. Share transfers must be entered in the shareholder ledger and reflected in the annual UBO filing, stating the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner(s). The UBO information must be kept up-to-date in the company's internal register and separately notified to DIAN/Chamber of Commerce within the annual filing window (by March 31).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Socios o Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Legal Representatives (Libro de Registro de Directivos y Representantes)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 150 – 400 per year for a commercial registered office address in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali; it can reach 800 – 1,500 if corporate secretarial support is included.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,200 – 2,500 for a statutory audit of a small/mid-sized SAS if thresholds are met; if no audit is required, accounting preparation and compliance services typically range from 300 – 800.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No preferential income tax rate for cotton brokerage/export trading; standard 35% applies. Colombia does not grant a general export tax holiday for this ISIC sector. VAT on exports is generally zero-rated, yielding cash-flow relief only. No CIT holiday or special export incentive applies to a Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada engaged in pure raw cotton bale export brokerage.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios for legal entities; filed electronically through the DIAN MUISCA electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; tax year is the calendar year (1 January – 31 December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment deadlines are fixed annually by DIAN Resolution according to the taxpayer's NIT last two digits, generally starting mid-September and ending in late October of the following year. No extensions are granted; the applicable filing date must be observed for both return and payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income received or accrued during the tax year, including brokerage commissions, export sales, and ancillary fees from raw cotton bale transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report amounts in Colombian pesos using the representative market exchange rate on the date of accrual/receipt; include the foreign buyer or seller's NIT when applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, discounts, and rebates granted to customers which reduce gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include discounts supported by credit notes or documentary evidence; discounts to related foreign entities must comply with arm's length principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 – Ingresos no constitutivos de renta
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items legally excluded from taxable income, e.g., certain indemnities or capital reimbursements; not generally applicable to ordinary export brokerage income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not characterize export proceeds as non-taxable income; foreign-source passive income may have separate treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of the raw cotton bales sold, including purchase cost, import/export logistics, freight, insurance, and port handling.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be supported with invoices, customs documents, and proof of payment; costs paid to foreign related parties are subject to transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, commissions, storage, insurance, administrative expenses, financial expenses, depreciation, and other deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service payments require withholding tax certificates and economic substance documentation; inflated or undocumented costs will be rejected by DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income; not normally available to cotton bale export trading companies under general Colombian CIT rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim exemptions unless a specific legal provision applies and is properly evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net ordinary income after deducting costs and expenses from gross income and adding net capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the accounting income adjusted for all CIT disallowances and limitations; foreign exchange gains/losses on export receivables must be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses carried forward to offset current net taxable income; Colombian law permits a 12-year carryforward, with no carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply losses chronologically; substantiate the history of prior tax returns if DIAN claims expiration or use in excess of the statutory limit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base after all applicable deductions, exemptions, and prior-year loss compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the base for the 35% CIT rate; non-resident shareholders should verify that the amount is not artificially reduced by transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 35% of the taxable income base; generally the largest annual cash liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No reduced rate applies for foreign-owned SAS; check DTA or domestic foreign-tax-credit rules for offsets if foreign permanent establishment income is included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits against income tax, such as taxes paid abroad under a DTA, investments with special deduction, or withholding taxes already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim a foreign tax credit, obtain an official foreign tax certificate and attach documentation showing the tax was actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT payable after tax credits and prepayments; if positive, must be paid with the Form 110 return or through DIAN payment systems.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that advance payments (retenciones en la fuente) are reconciled and that no amount due remains unpaid after the filing deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due for each month or fraction of delay, up to 100% of the tax due. If no tax is due, the penalty is 1% of gross income, capped at 10,000 UVT. Default interest accrues daily on unpaid tax at the DIAN rate. Inaccurate returns are subject to an additional inexactitud penalty of up to 100% of the difference between the correct tax and the declared tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% general withholding tax rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders out of profits that have already been taxed at the corporate level; DTA provisions may further reduce this rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a tax treaty reduction, the foreign beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority and provide it to the Colombian payor before payment. The payor must automatically withhold at the statutory rate unless a valid treaty claim is documented. The Colombian payer should retain the TRC, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the relevant treaty article reference in case DIAN audits the withholding. Refunds for excessive withholding can be claimed through the annual income tax return or specific DIAN refunds procedure if an overpayment arises.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and technical assistance/technology transfer payments: statutory withholding tax 15% on gross remittances. Interest payments: statutory withholding tax 15% generally; treaty-concluded rates can reduce royalties and interest to 10-15% and 0-10% respectively, depending on the foreign lender's status and treaty terms.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is generally triggered when the taxpayer's gross income or total assets exceed 100,000 UVT in the prior year and the taxpayer executes reportable related-party cross-border transactions. For 2025, the UVT is COP 49,799, making the main threshold approximately COP 4,979.9 million. Separate filing thresholds for the Colombian TP information return (Form 120) and CbC report are set annually in UVT; operators must recompute based on current-year UVT even if their raw cotton export transactions are low-volume.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply offshore economic substance regulations as such, but enforces substance-oriented anti-avoidance rules. A ‘sociedad no operativa’ (shell company) is subject to renta presuntiva, currently 3.5% of net equity, and may have costs disallowed if it lacks actual commercial and operational substance. The GAAR (general anti-abuse rule), CFC regime, and transfer pricing rules can also reclassify or eliminate artificial structures. For an SAS engaged in raw cotton bales export brokerage, the company must maintain real staff, office/logistical capacity, bank accounts, contracts, invoices, and risk exposure; an entity that only acts as a pass-through commission channel for a foreign parent will be challenged by DIAN.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Income Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Inaccuracy
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting export brokerage income from raw cotton bales, inflating costs through interposed suppliers, recording personal expenses as trade deductions, or omitting foreign bank accounts and export receivables from the annual tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanción por inexactitud under Article 647 E.T. of up to 100% of the tax difference; correction of taxable income; default interest at the DIAN rate; criminal tax evasion charges under Ley 1762/2015 can lead to significant fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and directors who knowingly sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt, subject to asset freezes, travel bans, disqualification, civil restitution, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the CO_SAS as a nominee entity with no physical office, employees, warehouse, or commercial risk; using the entity solely to invoice cotton exports or create artificial deductions without actual trade functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Renta presuntiva of 3.5% on net equity, disallowance of deductions, application of GAAR to redetermine taxable income, and potential administrative cancellation or penalty under commercial registry rules; tax debt becomes due with interest and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the resulting tax debt if they approved the shell structure; travel restrictions, asset embargoes, and criminal liability for fraudulent insolvency or asset stripping may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 120 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) or the required Local/Master File; setting export prices or commissions with related foreign cotton mills or trading affiliates below arm's length; using no comparability analysis or TP study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may adjust the taxpayer's income to arm's length, assessing additional CIT at 35% plus default interest. Failure to file TP documentation triggers penalties under Article 651 E.T., up to 15,000 UVT; false data can also trigger an inaccuracy penalty up to 100% of the resulting tax deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete or false TP documentation are exposed to personal fines, disqualification, asset freezes, and criminal proceedings if the false documentation is used to avoid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering and Customs False Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a conduit for money laundering through over/under-invoicing cotton bales; accepting third-party payments unrelated to actual cotton sales; splitting export proceeds to avoid reporting thresholds; using shell overseas buyers in high-risk jurisdictions for no commercial reason.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Colombian money-laundering law (Law 599/2000, Article 323) provides long imprisonment terms; foreign trade penalties under customs legislation (Decree 1165/2019) include fines, seizure of goods, and cancellation of exporter registration; SAR/MLRO failures carry administrative sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal liability, personal fines, civil confiscation, travel bans, and disqualification from managing commercial companies; the corporate veil may be pierced to recover laundered assets.
